title: Concierge: task conductor for privileged admin utilities and runbook-as-tasks
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a 'Concierge' coordinator service that exposes composable, auditable task flows for internal admin utilities. The goal is to convert existing ad-hoc scripts and multi-step runbooks into first-class tasks with guarded execution, RBAC checks, dry-run mode, and structured telemetry. This will let support engineers and SREs run common recovery operations (e.g., resync KV cache, invalidate prefixes, scale a dedicated pool, promote fallback model variants) as single-click tasks in the Console and via the admin CLI, while preserving an audit trail and safe defaults.
background: Over the last 18 months we've accumulated many one-off admin scripts and runbooks. Operators are running varied sequences manually during incidents; that causes variance in outcomes and missing telemetry. We need a unified conductor that: 1) treats runbooks as parameterized tasks, 2) enforces least privilege and approval flows for dangerous steps, and 3) emits structured events to the ops dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: Concierge service deployed to staging and reachable from Console and ops CLI
At least five canonical runbooks converted to task flows (cache-invalidate, model-variant-fallback, restart-worker-group, rotate-service-credentials read-only dry-run)
RBAC enforcement: only users in 'ops-admin' or with explicit approval token can run destructive steps
Every task execution generates a structured audit event with requestor, params, step-by-step outcomes and a link to the execution trace
Dry-run mode executes validation steps without performing state changes and returns deterministic preflight report
Canary rollout to a subset of internal teams and automated rollback on regressions
Comprehensive E2E tests and unit coverage for the conductor core, plus integration tests with the admin-auth and telemetry pipelines
implementation_notes: Architecture: lightweight coordinator (Go) that orchestrates idempotent step handlers (K8s jobs or lambda-like workers). Use existing opsctl agent for triggering and capturing stdout/stderr.
Task DSL: JSON/YAML first-class task definitions with parameters, validators, preconditions, compensation (undo) hooks and estimated cost metadata
Secrets: wire into KMS-backed short-lived credentials; destructive steps require ephemeral approval tokens issued by the approvals service
Telemetry: emit execution events to the ops-event bus with schema ops.concierge.execution.v1
Observability: expose per-task traces, step timings, and token-level cost estimate to Console. Add new dashboard tile in ops console: Concierge > Recent Runs
Failure handling: each step can declare retry semantics and fallback alternatives; orchestrator must support automatic rollback if compensation hooks are provided
security_considerations: Require mTLS for conductor <-> worker communication
Restrict which tasks are instantiable in production via allowlists
Audit immutable logs stored in write-once S3 bucket for 1 year
Approval tokens expire in 10 minutes and are single-use
Pen-test scope: include conductor, task templates, and approval flow
rollout_plan: MVP: internal staging only with feature-flagged Console actions (2 weeks)
Pilot: invite SRE, Oncall rotation, and two Product teams for early feedback (4 weeks)
Gradual enablement: enable for all internal teams, disable destructive steps for non-admins (6 weeks)
GA: enable in production for ops-admin role and add self-serve templates in Console (10 weeks)
migration_plan: Inventory current scripts and map to DSL patterns (owners assigned)
Convert high-frequency incident steps first (cache ops, model fallback)
Deprecate legacy scripts with redirect warnings in ops docs
Provide CLI shim that translates old script invocations into Concierge task invocations for backward compatibility
